transcript.text: What's the main goal you'd like this plan to support?
I want to finish a 50K trail race in 16 weeks.
When you picture this plan working, what does it look like? For example: start with some easy jogging, then build up to longer runs.
Add a long trail run on weekends, build it up gradually, and add hills and time on my feet.

Your goal, in your words: "I want to finish a 50K trail race in 16 weeks." Your recorded history covers 180 days. Your longest qualified continuous block is 63.0 minutes. In that time you've recorded 145 runs and 24 strength sessions. Your four-week jog average is 318.2 minutes per week. Your consistent jogging and strength work mean you already have the durable foundation needed to build toward finishing a trail ultra. How would you describe where you are with your activity right now?
That matches what I have been doing. Mostly road so far.
Which days and time of day are realistically available for you?
Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday mornings.
What kinds of exercise do you enjoy, and is there anything you'd rather avoid? For example: running and walking, but no gym.
Trail running and hiking are my favorites, and I do some lifting once a week.
Do you have any injuries or health conditions we should plan around?
Nothing to report.
It sounds like there's nothing we need to plan around — is that right? Say yes or tell me what I missed.
Yes, that is right.
How would you like me to communicate—plain, warm, or terse, and brief or full?
Warm and brief.
Here's how the plan will run: we check in every Monday, and I plan 4 weeks at a time, building toward 2026-12-21. Does that work, or would you like to change anything?
Let's check in on Mondays, 4 weeks at a time.
Here's how the plan will run: we check in every Monday, and I plan 4 weeks at a time, building toward 2026-12-21. Does that work now, or anything else to change?
Yes, sounds good.
